title: Ethanol Tolerance Assay Experiment in 96-well Plates
author: Daniel Olson
materials: Make duplicates of fresh ethanol standard solutions in water to be used during the growth (anaerobic) and the ethanol final measurement (Aerobic).

Check if you have buffer solutions (glycine buffer, ADH (Enzyme solution), and NAD stock solution) for the ethanol concentration assay. If not, make fresh buffers use milli-Q water, and store at the appropriate temperatures as indicated in the accompanying excel sheet.
After the growth plate has completed (5 days).

steps.title: Check and prepare supplies
steps.instruction: Inside the anaerobic chamber verify that plasticware, combi tips, a 96‑well growth plate, pipette tips and film covers are present and re‑supply if needed, opening package corners before passing through the airlock; confirm sufficient growth media or prepare fresh media and bring it into the chamber; locate mid‑log freezer stocks of the test strains (frozen in the same media) or start overnight cultures if stocks are unavailable; at the bench collect 1–1.5 mL pure ethyl alcohol with a needle and syringe from the stock bottle and dispense it into a 1.5 mL or 2 mL tube.

substeps.instruction: Verify plasticware, combi tips, 96‑well plate, pipette tips, and film covers inside the chamber; open package corners before airlock entry.
Check growth‑media volume; if insufficient, prepare fresh media and bring it into the chamber to remove oxygen.
Locate mid‑log freezer stocks of strains frozen in the same media; if absent, inoculate overnight cultures.
Collect 1–1.5 mL pure ethyl alcohol with a needle‑syringe and dispense into a 1.5 mL or 2 mL tube.

steps.title: Prepare anaerobic chamber atmosphere
steps.instruction: Fill the chamber with the prescribed gas mix and nitrogen until the hydrogen concentration reaches ≥ 2 % and the oxygen reading is 0 ppm; if oxygen is high, vacuum the chamber, refill with nitrogen and gas mix, and continue topping off as the chamber deflates, repeating until hydrogen is ≥ 2 % and oxygen is 0 ppm.

substeps.instruction: Introduce gas mix and nitrogen; monitor hydrogen until ≥ 2 %.
Check oxygen; if >0 ppm, evacuate air, refill with nitrogen and gas mix.
Top‑off the chamber repeatedly as pressure drops.
Re‑verify that H₂ ≥ 2 % and O₂ = 0 ppm before proceeding.

steps.title: Make media aliquots with antibiotics
steps.instruction: Prepare aliquots of growth media with or without antibiotics for plate filling; when using antibiotics, add enough concentrated antibiotic media so that 35 µL of this concentrate yields the desired final antibiotic concentration in a 200 µL well.

steps.title: Transfer stocks and equipment into chamber
steps.instruction: Bring frozen mid‑log working stocks of the test strains into the anaerobic chamber together with a repeat pipette, a 1.0–10.0 µL multichannel pipette, and a 96‑well plate that already contains 50 µL dH₂O per well and is sealed with a film for the initial ethanol‑assay samples.

steps.title: Initialize growth‑curve software and heat reader
steps.instruction: At the computer adjacent to the chamber, open GEN5 3.11, check the signup sheet, press “Read Now”, select the “Dan 1 growth curve protocol 120 hrs”, press OK, and allow the plate reader to warm to 55 °C while you prepare the plate.

steps.title: Set up growth plate with cultures
steps.instruction: In the anaerobic chamber rinse a combi tip three times with plain media, then using a 100 µL combi tip add 2.0 µL frozen culture to each strain‑designated well with a multichannel pipette; keep the freezer vial on ice and discard after the assay. Carefully add 200 µL growth media to wells in columns 2–11 using a 2.5 mL combi tip set to a dispensing volume of ≤#6, dispensing at an angle to the side of the well to avoid splashing. If fewer than ten strains are tested, leave the remaining wells empty.

substeps.instruction: Rinse combi tip 3× with plain media.
Add 2.0 µL frozen culture to designated wells (multichannel, 100 µL tip).
Keep stock vial on ice; discard after use.
Add 200 µL growth media to columns 2–11 (2.5 mL tip, dispense ≤#6, angled).
Leave extra wells empty when <10 strains are used.

steps.title: Prepare initial ethanol assay plate
steps.instruction: Set up a separate 96‑well plate inside the chamber by adding 50 µL dH₂O to each well, keep the sealing film on, then remove the film to expose the wells for sample addition.

steps.title: Add ethanol samples to assay plate
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette add 5.0 µL of each ethanol‑assay sample to its corresponding well, then gently place the sealing film back on the plate without pressing too firmly so it can be removed later for standard addition.

steps.title: Seal and start growth plate run
steps.instruction: Seal the initial test plate with an RTS film using a rubber roller or tape, place the sealed plate into the plate holder (no plastic lid), insert it with the A1 corner at the back/right corner of the holder, and press OK in the software pop‑up to move the plate into the reader and begin the 120‑hour growth curve.

steps.title: Monitor growth and defrost assay reagents
steps.instruction: Periodically check the plate‑reader software to ensure the run is continuing; one hour before the 120‑hour growth curve ends, defrost the ethanol‑assay aliquots (NAD and ADH) on ice.

steps.title: Start ethanol assay software on aerobic reader
steps.instruction: On the computer linked to the aerobic plate reader, launch the ethanol‑assay protocol and let the instrument warm to 30 °C; leave a sign on the reader indicating the assay is in progress so it is not turned off, then promptly move to the reader after adding assay buffer to read the samples.

steps.title: Prepare and run ethanol concentration assay plate
steps.instruction: On ice, mix the assay‑buffer components in a 50 mL Falcon tube; add 5.0 µL standard sample to wells in columns 1 and 12 to generate a standard curve; using a multichannel pipette quickly add 190 µL assay buffer to all wells of a new 96‑well plate, seal with film using a rubber roller, place the plate in the reader holder with A1 corner at the back/right, and click OK in the pop‑up to start the read.

substeps.instruction: Mix assay buffer in 50 mL Falcon tube on ice.
Add 5.0 µL standard to columns 1 and 12 for standard curve.
Add 190 µL assay buffer to all wells (multichannel).
Insert plate (A1 corner back/right) and start read.
